subject: social_science
chapter_title: Gender, Religion and Caste in Democratic Politics

concepts.title: Public Private Division and Feminist Movements
concepts.definition: Society splits life into a public world of work and politics run mostly by men, and a private household world where unpaid labour falls on women, and feminist movements arose to demand equal political and legal rights for women against this patriarchal division.
concepts.key_idea: An average Indian woman works one hour more than an average man every day, yet much of her work is unpaid and therefore unvalued, which is why housework remains invisible.
question_patterns: what does the public private division mean
why is the work of women in the household not valued
what are feminist movements
why do we call indian society patriarchal
explain the time use survey of household work
how does an average woman's working day compare with a man's

solution_steps.explain: Identify paid, public activity against unpaid, household activity and see which gender occupies each.
Use the time-use survey idea: record hours on income work, household work, care and rest, then compare men and women.
Confirm that feminists sought equal rights and political voice, treating women's problems as matters of power, not charity.

concepts.title: Literacy Gap between Women and Men
concepts.definition: Women's literacy trails men's by the difference of the two literacy rates, and this gap in percentage points captures gender disadvantage in education.
concepts.key_idea: With women's literacy at 54 per cent against men's 76 per cent, the gap of about 22 percentage points shows why girls drop out as parents prefer spending on boys.
question_patterns: calculate the gap between male and female literacy rates
how many percentage points do women trail men in literacy
find the literacy gap when both rates are given
compare women's and men's literacy rates in india
why do girls drop out of school more than boys

solution_steps.explain: Take the male literacy rate and subtract the female literacy rate to get the gap in percentage points

concepts.title: Child Sex Ratio from Births Data
concepts.definition: The child sex ratio counts girl children per thousand boys, found by dividing the number of girls by the number of boys and scaling to a thousand; sex-selective abortion has pushed the ratio down to 919 nationally and below 850 in some states.
concepts.key_idea: Preference for sons and misuse of technology have made the ratio fall below 850 or even 800 in some states, as the Census 2011 map shows.
question_patterns: calculate the child sex ratio from the number of girls and boys
how many girl children are there per thousand boys
find the sex ratio when the counts of girls and boys are given
what is the child sex ratio of india according to census 2011
why has the child sex ratio declined in india
identify states where the child sex ratio is below 900

solution_steps.action: scale girls to a thousand boys
solution_steps.explain: Divide the number of girl children by the number of boy children and multiply by 1000

concepts.title: Women's Political Representation and Reservation
concepts.definition: Women's share in legislatures stays very low, touching 14.36 per cent of the Lok Sabha only in 2019 and under 5 per cent in state assemblies, which is why feminists demand reservation, and panchayats and municipalities already reserve at least one-third of seats for women.
concepts.key_idea: The Equal Remuneration Act of 1976 promises equal wages for equal work, but reservation of elected seats is seen as the surest way to let women control power and attention to their problems.
question_patterns: what per cent of the lok sabha members are women after 2019
why is women's representation in legislature so low
what reservation do women have in panchayats and municipalities
what does the equal remuneration act provide
why do feminists demand reservation of seats for women
compare women's share in lok sabha and state assemblies

solution_steps.explain: Record the 14.36 per cent Lok Sabha share in 2019 and the under 5 per cent share in assemblies.
Cite the one-third reservation in local bodies and the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 as existing measures.
Only when women control power will their problems get adequate attention, the reasoning behind reservation demands.

concepts.title: Communalism and Its Forms
concepts.definition: Communalism treats followers of one religion as a single political community with interests opposed to others, ranging from everyday beliefs in the superiority of one's religion to majoritarian dominance and finally to communal riots and violence.
concepts.key_idea: A communal mind sees one's own religion as superior and the nation as an expression of one major religion, and the ugliest form appeared in communal riots at the time of the partition of the country.
question_patterns: what is communalism
describe the different forms of communalism
how does communalism take the form of riots and violence
what does a communal mind believe
how does communalism use religion in politics
give examples of communal prejudices in everyday life

solution_steps.explain: Order the stages: everyday fanaticism, desire for majority dominance, political mobilisation on religious lines, and violence or riots.
Communalism claims followers of one religion share identical secular interests, which is historically false.
Link the ugliest form toPartition and communal riots like those at the time of independence.

concepts.title: Secularism in the Indian Constitution
concepts.definition: India chose a secular constitutional model with no official state religion: the Constitution gives individuals and communities freedom to profess and practise their religion, and bars discrimination on religious grounds.
concepts.key_idea: Unlike states that protect one religion, the Indian Constitution works through three strategies of non-interference, accommodation and non-discrimination, making secularism more than a mere ideology.
question_patterns: why is india called a secular state
which constitutional provisions make india secular
how does the indian constitution prevent religious discrimination
compare indian secularism with states having an official religion
what is the difference between communal and secular politics
why does combating communalism need a secular constitution

solution_steps.action: check the absence of state religion
solution_steps.explain: Confirm no religion is declared the official religion of the Indian state.
Freedom to profess, practise and propagate religion, equality before law, and no discrimination on grounds of religion.
The state may intervene to end a religious social evil while keeping distance from religion as such.

concepts.title: Caste Inequalities: SC, ST and OBC Shares
concepts.definition: Census data show the Scheduled Castes at 16.6 per cent and the Scheduled Tribes at 8.6 per cent of the population, while the National Sample Survey puts Other Backward Classes at around 41 per cent, so together these groups form about two-thirds of the country.
concepts.key_idea: The Census does not count OBCs separately; caste untouchability is outlawed but its economic effects persist, and urban life weakens caste's daily grip.
question_patterns: what share of india's population do the scheduled castes and tribes form
what per cent of the population are other backward classes according to the nss
who are dalits and adivasis
how do sc st and obc together add up to two thirds of the population
why does the census not count obcs
how did the constitution address caste discrimination

solution_steps.explain: SC 16.6 per cent and ST 8.6 per cent come from Census 2011; OBC around 41 per cent comes from the NSS 2004-05.
Together SC, ST and OBC make about two-thirds of the population and three-fourths of the Hindu population.
Scheduled Castes are those earlier treated as outcaste and subjected to untouchability; Scheduled Tribes are communities that lived secluded in hills and forests.

concepts.title: Casteism in Electoral Politics
concepts.definition: Caste enters politics when parties choose candidates and constituencies with caste arithmetic in mind, yet no parliamentary constituency has a single-caste majority, so candidates must appeal beyond one caste to win.
concepts.key_idea: Universal adult franchise and one-person-one-vote pushed political leaders to mobilise caste groups, but no caste can win an election alone in most constituencies.
question_patterns: how does casteism appear in electoral politics
can any single caste dominate a constituency's voters
how do parties use caste while selecting candidates
why does universal adult franchise affect caste politics
does the expression of caste difference become casteism always
explain how no constituency has a single caste majority

solution_steps.explain: Candidate choice, caste associations in campaigns, and appeal to caste sentiment in voting.
No parliamentary constituency has a single-caste majority, so victory needs coalitions of castes and communities.
Caste difference is usual in society; it turns into casteism only when used to deny dignity or equal treatment.

concepts.title: Combined Share of Backward Groups
concepts.definition: The combined population share of several social groups is the sum of their individual shares, so the SC, ST and OBC populations can be added as percentages of the whole country.
concepts.key_idea: Adding 16.6 per cent, 8.6 per cent and roughly 41 per cent yields about two-thirds of the population belonging to SC, ST and OBC groups.
question_patterns: calculate the combined population share of sc st and obc groups
what percentage do the scheduled groups add up to
find the total share when group percentages are given
compute the sum of sc st and obc shares of population
how much of india's population belongs to backward groups together

solution_steps.explain: Sum the percentage shares of the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes
